_comment: Mutation testing for the optional-feature flag resolver. featureFlags.js is a small file that decides something consequential: whether a stored WorkerConfig override wins over an env-var default, per flag. A test that merely executed those lines would still pass if the precedence were inverted, so line coverage says nothing here — mutation does. Scoped to src/featureFlags.js and its OWN unit test (vitest.stryker.features.config.js), which is fully mocked and reads no real filesystem, so it runs clean inside Stryker's app/api-only sandbox. Run: cd app/api && npm run test:mutation:features. MUTATION FLOOR: `break` is set a few points under the measured score and is a RATCHET — it only goes up. Enforced by the weekly .github/workflows/js-mutation.yml, never on a PR. Raise it when the score rises; never lower it to make a red run green — a drop means a test stopped discriminating. Measured 100.0% when the floor was set to 98.

mutationExclusions.src/ingest/systemBoundary.js: Not yet measured. Added by SEC-2026-09 (per-system ingest boundary). Stryker could not produce an honest score on the workstation this was written on: its vitest runner does not activate mutants there (this config’s own src/featureFlags.js scored 18.5% locally against the 100% measured in CI), so any number quoted here would be wrong. The decisions in this file are pinned by its own fully-mocked unit test with discriminating inputs; the ingest boundary it serves is also exercised end to end against a real schema by contract-tests/ingestSystemBoundary.integration.test.js. Measure it on Linux and move it into a scope’s mutate list.
